subject.title: fix(agents): skip error classification for clean non-zero exits

question: Should OpenClaw preserve the current rule that ordinary non-zero exits warn, or add a new explicit accepted-exit contract for commands whose non-zero result is intentionally non-failing?
rationale: `completed` currently describes how the process terminated, not whether the command succeeded, so source inspection cannot infer which non-zero results maintainers want channels to suppress.

options.title: Add accepted-exit contract
options.body: Keep non-zero warnings by default and suppress them only when exec emits an explicit accepted outcome, with regression and live channel proof.

options.title: Keep current warnings
options.body: Reject the global suppression and require commands that expect non-zero results to normalize their shell status, such as with an intentional fallback.

options.title: Suppress all normal exits
options.body: Adopt the PR's rule and accept that genuine failures with exit codes 1-125 will no longer produce channel warnings.

recommendation.title: Add accepted-exit contract
recommendation.body: Keep non-zero warnings by default and suppress them only when exec emits an explicit accepted outcome, with regression and live channel proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available low-confidence routing candidate for the shared agents runtime and user-visible tool-warning contract.
